newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dlr/yen risk reversals flip for yen puts.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr/yen risk reversals flip for yen puts.

text.p: Shorter-dated yen puts in dollar/yen options were bid up above equivalent yen calls on Monday for the first time since the spot dollar fell from its May highs, traders said.
Risk reversals, the cost of swapping equally out-of-the-money puts and calls, flipped in favor of yen puts in the one-month area as the dollar rallied past resistance in the 117 area, they said.
"I think we're hitting significant enough levels and people are believing spot's going to go higher," said John Bird, senior currency options analyst at Technical Data.
The 117-yen area had previously capped the dollar's bounces in the past few months after the U.S. unit fell to within a whisker of the 110-yen level.
One-month 25-delta risk reversal were 0.0/0.3 percentage point skewed for yen puts today against 0.3/0.7 in favor of yen calls late on Friday.
About a month ago, when the market was fixated with the dollar's downside risk, the one-month 25-delta traded as wided as 3.0 point in favor of yen calls.
Longer-dated risk reversals were still marginally favoring yen calls, traders said.
However, implied volatilities in absolute terms were bid more aggressively in the back end than in the front end, noted Masao Okada, chief options dealer at Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank.
"It's not that there's that much demand for gamma," he said, adding that spot had not moved extraordinarily after finishing just beneath 117 yen last Friday.
Shorter-dated options have higher gamma, which provides quicker premium acceleration and bigger delta swings, but are more vulnerable to time decay.
"A lot of dealers got their offers taken in the back-end," Okada said.

"It's become too expensive to cover short vega positions in those maturities, so bids rolled over to the front end," he added. Longer-dated options have higher vega, the rate of change in premiums per change in implied volatility, and thus are more painful to short-cover when volatilities are higher.
One-month dollar/yen volatility stood at 10.9/11.1 percent in early afternoon U.S., up from 10.0/10.3 late on Friday. One-year rose about 0.6 point to 11.6/11.8 percent.
The curve-wide surge in volatilities was making the front end vulnerable to a pullback should spot start to consolidate, Okada added.
Dollar/mark volatilities were barely changed, despite the dollar's advance to fresh 7-1/2 year highs toward 1.85 marks.
One-month out to six-month were all pegged at 10.4/10.7 percent. One-month 25-delta risk reversal stood at 0.6/0.9 point in favor of mark puts.
With spot continuing to grind up very steadily, traders said volatilities were likely to remain flat.
"I think it all depends on the speed with which we get there (new highs)," Bird said.
Elsewhere, sterling/mark volatilities were well bid as the pound tumbled after a big bull run in recent weeks.
-- Shin Kishima/Chicago Derivatives Desk ((312-408-8750))
E-mail: derivatives@reuters.com
